original_question: Let K be a number field, let f (x), g(x) ∈ K[x] be polynomials of degree at least 2, and let a, b ∈ K. (a) Suppose that for all but finitely many primes p, the mod p orbits of a and b satisfy (22.1) Of˜(ã mod p) ∩ Og̃ (b̃ mod p) 6= ∅. Is it true that true that f and g have the same complex Julia sets? 33 If the answer is affirmative, does it suffice to assume that (22.1) holds for a set of primes of density 1? (b) Fix some ǫ > 0, and suppose that the intersection (22.1) has at least Npǫ elements for infinitely many primes p. Is it true that true that f and g have the same complex Julia sets? 33Aside from power maps and Chebyshev polynomials, having the same Julia set is more-or-less equivalent to f and g having a common iterate, up to symmetries of the Julia set.
target_in_paper: Section 22, Question 22.4(a)–(b), including equation (22.1) and footnote 33. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper: it correctly identifies the ambient objects (a number field K, polynomials f and g of degree at least 2, and points a,b in K), reproduces the mod-p orbit-intersection condition (22.1), keeps both the density-1 follow-up in part (a) and the quantitative strengthening in part (b), and preserves the paper’s footnote-level motivation relating common Julia sets to common iterates outside exceptional families. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the phrase "complex Julia sets" should specify that K is being viewed through a fixed embedding K ↪ C; otherwise one has not said in which complex plane the Julia sets are taken. The paper leaves this implicit. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Because K is a number field, "mod p" should be unpacked as reduction at non-archimedean primes (prime ideals) 𝔭 of O_K outside a finite bad-reduction set, so that the reductions of f, g, a, and b are actually defined. The paper states this informally as "primes p." ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The forward-orbit notation should be defined explicitly: for any map h, O_h(c) = {h^n(c) : n ≥ 0}. That notation is introduced earlier in the paper and is used implicitly in Question 22.4. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

If one wants the density-1 clause to be self-contained over a number field, one should say what density means for the relevant primes; the paper defines natural density earlier (for primes in Z), but does not restate it in Question 22.4. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

In part (b), the OCR-style string "Np^ε" is not self-explanatory in isolation; in a stand-alone restatement it should be written unambiguously as a lower bound in terms of the residue-field size or prime norm, e.g. (N𝔭)^ε where N𝔭 = #(O_K/𝔭). This clarification is forced by the number-field setting of Question 22.4. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The question is meant as a local-global formulation of the Dynamical Mordell–Lang problem, so that contextual intent is worth stating explicitly when sharpening the draft. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
refined_question: Let K be a number field, viewed via a fixed embedding K ↪ C. Let f,g ∈ K[x] be polynomials of degree at least 2, and let a,b ∈ K. For each nonzero prime ideal 𝔭 of O_K outside a finite set large enough that the reductions f mod 𝔭, g mod 𝔭, a mod 𝔭, and b mod 𝔭 are defined, write O_h(c) = {h^n(c) : n ≥ 0} for a forward orbit, let f̃, g̃, ã, b̃ denote the corresponding reductions modulo 𝔭, and let N𝔭 = #(O_K/𝔭). Is the following local-global statement true? (a) If O_f̃(ã) ∩ O_g̃(b̃) ≠ ∅ for all but finitely many such primes 𝔭, must f and g have the same Julia set in C? If so, does the same conclusion already follow when this nonempty-intersection condition holds for a set of primes 𝔭 of natural density 1? (b) Fix ε > 0. If #(O_f̃(ã) ∩ O_g̃(b̃)) ≥ (N𝔭)^ε for infinitely many such primes 𝔭, must f and g have the same Julia set in C?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Question 22.4, not any of the opening conjectures: it quotes the exact equation number (22.1), the two-part structure, the density-1 follow-up, and footnote 33 about Julia sets versus common iterates. The sentence immediately preceding Question 22.4 says that it is "another local-global formulation of dynamical Mordell–Lang," and the earlier Dynamical Mordell–Lang material in Section 7—especially Theorem 7.4 on orbit intersections of polynomials—explains why the intended global conclusion is a strong dynamical relation between f and g. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
